title: Compatible geometric evaluations and regular-module scalars
statement: Let E be a totally disconnected normed field, X,V,W schemes, p:V to X and g:W to X morphisms, and a:Spec(Omega) to V and d:Spec(Omega) to W morphisms for an algebraically closed field Omega, with a composed with p equal to d composed with g. Fix z in Spec(Omega). Put R equal to the condensed E coefficient ring on X, Ri=p inverse image R and Rj=g inverse image R. There exist additive finite-colimit-preserving functors F:Mod(Ri) to E-vector spaces and G:Mod(Rj) to E-vector spaces, and a natural isomorphism between pullback_p followed by F and pullback_g followed by G. There are E-linear equivalences b:F(regular Ri) to E and c:G(regular Rj) to E. For every endomorphism f of regular Ri, b(F(f)(b inverse of 1)) is the value at a(z) of the continuous coefficient obtained by conjugating the underlying endomorphism by condensedFieldPullbackRealization and applying its global sections to 1; the corresponding G statement holds at d(z). The coefficients and realization are those of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-field-presentation-matrix]. No chosen module, finite presentation, matrix rank or corank equality appears in this theorem.

proof.text: Extend scalars along the canonical coefficient isomorphism for p or g, then apply module inverse image along a or d. Both routes land over the condensed coefficient ring on Spec(Omega). Evaluate the underlying abelian sheaf and its internal action at the terminal object. The continuous realization identifies the scalar ring with ULift E because Spec(Omega) has one point. Define the ordinary E-action by applying the internal action to ULift(e) tensor m; the tensor universal property, internal unit and associativity equations, and internal linearity diagrams supply the module and functor laws. All covers of an algebraically closed field split, so abelian evaluation preserves cokernels. Finite colimits of internal modules are computed on underlying sheaves, and ordinary module forgetful functors reflect them, yielding preservation of finite colimits. Inverse image and coefficient change preserve finite colimits and are additive. The module inverse-image composition and coefficient comparisons, together with had, give the natural comparison on every module over X.

The regular coefficient module evaluates to E, with its ordinary scalar action obtained by evaluating the internal module action on pure tensors. This gives b and c. An endomorphism of the regular module is multiplication by its value on 1. The canonical continuous realization characterizes this coefficient as the conjugated regular-module endomorphism on global sections applied to 1. Its geometric pullback is the value of that function at a(z) or d(z). This proves the two scalar formulas. Arbitrary finite-free coordinates and the full matrix equations are proved in the parent, using only additivity and biproduct inclusions and projections.

theorem exists_condensedField_compatible_evaluations
    (E : Type u) [NormedField E] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace E]
    (X V W : Scheme.{u}) (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (p : V ⟶ X) (g : W ⟶ X)
    (a : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ V) (d : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ W)
    (had : a ≫ p = d ≫ g) (z : Spec (.of Ω)) :
    let R := condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousCoefficientRingObj E) X
    let Ri := (upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} p).obj R
    let Rj := (upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} g).obj R
    ∃ (F : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology V) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) Ri ⥤
        ModuleCat.{u + 1} E)
      (G : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology W) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) Rj ⥤
        ModuleCat.{u + 1} E),
      F.Additive ∧ G.Additive ∧ PreservesFiniteColimits F ∧ PreservesFiniteColimits G ∧
      Nonempty (((upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} p).mapMod R) ⋙ F ≅
        ((upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} g).mapMod R) ⋙ G) ∧
      ∃ (b : F.obj (Mod.regular Ri) ≃ₗ[E] E)
        (c : G.obj (Mod.regular Rj) ≃ₗ[E] E),
        (∀ f : Mod.regular Ri ⟶ Mod.regular Ri,
          b (F.map f (b.symm 1)) =
            (((inv (condensedFieldPullbackRealization E p) ≫ f.hom ≫
              condensedFieldPullbackRealization E p).hom.app
                (Opposite.op (Scheme.ProEt.mk (𝟙 V)))) (ULift.up 1)).down (a z)) ∧
        (∀ f : Mod.regular Rj ⟶ Mod.regular Rj,
          c (G.map f (c.symm 1)) =
            (((inv (condensedFieldPullbackRealization E g) ≫ f.hom ≫
              condensedFieldPullbackRealization E g).hom.app
                (Opposite.op (Scheme.ProEt.mk (𝟙 W)))) (ULift.up 1)).down (d z))
